release: MINOR: the product is now called Site Audit. SGEN is gone from every surface a user reads - window and report titles, the header brand, the manual, diagnostics, desktop notifications, the guided tour and the annotation report. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT RENAMED, because these are DATA PATHS and not display strings: NOTES_DIR in sgen-qa-serve.js still points at %APPDATA%\SGEN Site QA, where the operator's saved annotations already live. Renaming it would orphan them for no visible benefit - nobody reads that folder name. The same reasoning keeps appId as com.sgen.siteqa: it is the update identity and the Windows AppUserModelID that main.js sets to match, so changing it would break both the toast and the upgrade path over an invisible string. ONE COLLISION FIXED: the product is now called Site Audit and tool 1 is also called Site Audit, so the annotation eyebrow template rendered Site Audit followed by Site Audit. A duplicated word reads as a rendering bug even when the data behind it is correct. SHELL HALF NEEDS AN INSTALLER. package.json productName and the main.js window title are renamed in source but ship ONLY via the NSIS installer, never the engine feed - so the taskbar and window-chrome name change lands on the next installer build, not on this update. Because Electron derives userData from productName, that build carries a one-time migration that moves the entire data root - every hot engine, every stored report, saved settings and logs - from SGEN Site QA to Site Audit. Without it the app would boot looking brand new and silently rolled back to the bundled engine.
